note: PLACEHOLDER. Every params object here validates against the published opponent_research manifest input_schema (additionalProperties: false, $refs inlined the way publish_experiments.py inlines them), and every value is plausible, but nobody has dispatched one. So a verdict drawn from this list is a claim about the pipeline, not about the agent. EIGHT cases, and DEFAULT_JUDGE_CONFIG.gates.minCases is 20. A corpus verdict over this list therefore resolves CAN'T SAY however the judge voted, because the floor was set from measured agent non-determinism and eight runs measure that rather than the branch. Eight is deliberate and not a rounding error: one clean baseline plus seven single-axis variations is what one change can author honestly across nine agents. Whether to grow every list to 20 or to lower the floor is still open — do not read the shortfall as a decision. Varied along: whether the opponent is a known incumbent, a known challenger or of unknown incumbency (is_incumbent true / false / null), which is what the agent has to reason about before it trusts a page; hint richness, from a website plus social URLs down to nothing but a name, which decides whether discovery is a fetch or a search; whether the candidate platform is supplied in full, partially null, or null outright, since that is the only thing the contrasts can be framed against; a large-city race with heavy coverage against a rural county commission and a school board where almost nothing is written down; and how much of race_context is hydrated, because city and election_date are what disambiguate a same-named person in the wrong cycle. People are fictional placeholders in the house style (gp-webapp e2e-tests briefings.spec.ts uses 'Test Official'); this file is public, so no real person is named. States, cities, office titles and L2 voter file column names are real.
